steps.title: The phone app is now native
steps.body: The Android app is rebuilt natively: every area of Crundi in proper phone screens instead of a web page inside an app. It has the workbench with swipe columns, splits and full screen, chats with live embeds, players and pictures you can zoom, files with drag and drop, the kanban, notes and mind map, and Mini walking about. Notifications, bubbles and replying from them work as before. Update it from the Play Store or the latest release.

steps.title: Start a factory from an alert
steps.body: A webhook trigger gives a factory a public URL for things like Grafana alerts. Calls must carry its key or be signed with its secret. You write the change request with parts of the call, like {{payload.message}}, and anything a call leaves out just comes out empty. An idempotency key you choose, such as {{payload.groupKey}}, means a repeat is never handled twice. A new call that arrives while the run is going goes to its Manager, marked as mid-run, so it can decide if it is the same issue. The Manager always gets the full request.

steps.title: Background chats that start when called
steps.body: A background chat can now start when its URL is called instead of at a time: an alert from Grafana, a CI job. It is secured the same way as factory webhooks, the prompt reads the call with {{payload.message}}, and an idempotency key drops repeats. Calls that come in while it is still working go into the same chat, marked Mid-run. With One ongoing chat, every alert comes back to the same conversation, so it remembers the earlier ones.

steps.title: A Manager that checks in and steps in
steps.body: The Manager now looks over the run on a check-in ticker, every 5 minutes up to every few hours. You set how often in the factory, or leave it to the Manager. It can message someone in the middle of their step, or stop their turn to say it first, or tell them to wait. A job it hands out shows on the graph as a line to that person until the job is done.
